newsitem.title: UK: UK's IMRO fines Canada Life for rule breaches.
newsitem.headline: UK's IMRO fines Canada Life for rule breaches.

text.p: British investment management watchdog the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) on Thursday fined Canada Life Management (UK) Ltd 50,000 pounds ($81,800) for breaches of its rules.

It said Canada Life had agreed to a settle disciplinary proceedings for failing to invest customers money on time, incorrectly pricing unit trusts, failing to bank client money on time and not having adequate compliance arrangements between March 1995 and June 1996.
IMRO said Canada Life had paid compensation of 57,965 pounds to 901 unitholders and had also paid 18,843 pounds into unit trusts. Canada Life will also pay IMRO's costs of 23,392 pounds.
IMRO said Canada Life had failed to invest cash it had received from its Personal Equity Plan (PEP) and unit trust customers "as soon as reasonably practicable".
And it did not take sufficient steps to avoid seven of its unit trusts being incorrectly priced from August 1995 to June 1996, IMRO said.

Canada Life's other failings included not paying money received from customers' PEP and unit trust applications into a client money bank account by the next business day and not having effective compliance procedures. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
